capability_investigated:
WhisperProcessor feature extractor with a list input, and the batched
prompt/result contract of frozen.asr_backend.generate (one prompt row,
one result row per input window).
what_i_learned:
The processor accepts a list of raw-audio chunks and returns input_features
shaped (N, mels, frames); generate accepts [prompt]*N and returns N results
(results[i].sequences_ids[0]). The stub fed only the first 30 s, so all audio
past 0:30 was silently dropped — a pure deletion sink on long-form calls.
hypothesis:
Window the full audio into non-overlapping 30 s segments, decode them in one
batched generate call, and concatenate the per-window text. This recovers the
truncated tail that the single-window stub deleted, which should sharply cut
corpus_cer on the long-form 0715 batch.

capability_investigated:
The VRAM cost model of frozen.asr_backend.generate under a batched prompt
list — what CT2 Whisper allocates when given (N, mels, frames) features vs
a single row.
what_i_learned:
generate decodes the whole prompt batch concurrently, so passing all N 30 s
windows in one call allocates encoder+decoder state for every row at once and
OOMs on long calls. Feeding one window per generate call caps peak VRAM at
single-window cost while still recovering all audio past 0:30; the batched
list contract works but is not memory-safe for long-form here.
hypothesis:
Loop the windows sequentially — one processor() + generate() per 30 s chunk —
and join the decoded text. This fixes the iter-1 OOM crash while preserving
its deletion-sink fix, so the candidate actually scores.

capability_investigated:
The `prompts` argument of frozen.asr_backend.generate — specifically whether
the prompt token-id list can carry a `<|startofprev|>` continuity segment
before `<|startoftranscript|>`, and what results[0].sequences_ids[0] returns
that can be fed back as that prefix.
what_i_learned:
generate's prompt is a flat list of token ids, so it accepts more than the
static SOT prefix: prepending the `<|startofprev|>` id plus the previous
window's decoded sequences_ids gives the decoder cross-window context — the
native Whisper long-form conditioning path, which the pipeline had never
used. Until now every 30 s window decoded context-blind from a cold start.
hypothesis:
Carry each window's decoded token ids forward (capped to 200 tokens) as a
`<|startofprev|>` prefix on the next window. Restoring continuity across the
hard 30 s cuts should reduce the cold-start drift/repetition collapse that
truncates windows early, lifting length_ratio and cutting the 80% deletion
axis — strongest on continuous-speech files like the 233 s-span worst case.

capability_investigated:
The timestamp-token channel of frozen.asr_backend.generate's return value:
what results[0].sequences_ids[0] contains when <|notimestamps|> is removed
from the prompt, and how those ids encode audio position.
what_i_learned:
Dropping <|notimestamps|> puts the CT2 decoder in timestamp mode, so
sequences_ids[0] carries timestamp tokens (ids >= the <|0.00|> id, each step
= 0.02 s) interleaved with text — a return-value channel the pipeline was
stripping via skip_special_tokens and otherwise discarding. The last such
token marks where the decode stayed reliable in the 30 s window, giving a
data-driven seek position that the fixed +30 s split never had.
hypothesis:
Mid-utterance fixed-window cuts drive the deletion axis (del 80%, len 0.65)
by forcing cold restarts mid-word that drift/loop and drop tails. Advancing
the next window to the decoder's last emitted timestamp (clamped to a trusted
20–30 s range, else full-window) cuts at natural boundaries and re-decodes
the uncertain tail with a clean lead-in, recovering deleted span while
keeping window count ~1.5x the blind split.

capability_investigated:
The scores and no_speech_prob return channels of frozen.asr_backend.generate:
what results[0] carries when return_scores=True and return_no_speech_prob=True
are passed, and how CT2 routes sampling_temperature (sampling_topk=0 vs the
greedy default of 1).
what_i_learned:
generate's result object exposes scores (a length-normalized average log-prob
per returned hypothesis, scores[0] for beam_size=1) and no_speech_prob (a
scalar) only when those kwargs are set — both were stripped/ignored before.
scores[0] is directly comparable to Whisper's -1.0 confidence gate, giving a
per-window failure signal the pipeline never had. sampling_temperature only
perturbs the decode when sampling_topk=0 (full-distribution sampling); at the
default topk=1 the decode stays greedy regardless of temperature.
hypothesis:
Wrap each window's decode in Whisper's native temperature-fallback loop:
greedy first, and when scores[0] is below -1.0 re-decode the same window at
rising sampling temperatures (sampling_topk=0), keeping the highest-confidence
candidate; no_speech_prob>=0.6 short-circuits to avoid re-rolling silence into
hallucination. Collapsed greedy passes that dropped half a window — the source
of the residual deletion axis (del 67%, length_ratio 0.82) — get replaced by a
pass that covers the span.

capability_investigated:
The raw-waveform energy envelope of the `audio` argument itself — frame-level
RMS computed directly from the numpy input, never read before. All prior
windowing conditioned on token-side signals (fixed 30 s, then last-timestamp
seek); the acoustic boundary structure in the waveform was untouched.
what_i_learned:
A per-call silence floor (a low percentile of 20 ms frame-RMS over the whole
call) cleanly separates pauses from speech without any forbidden asset: the
silence-heavy files (silence_ratio 0.13-0.25) expose real troughs near the
30 s mark to cut at, while the worst file (silence_ratio 0.065, 181 s speech
runs) has none in its window tail — so a waveform-derived cut must degrade to
the timestamp seek there, not replace it.
hypothesis:
Snap each full window's end to the quietest sub-floor frame in its last 10 s
and advance to exactly that pause, so windows begin and end in silence and the
decoder never restarts cold mid-word at the seam — recovering deletion at
window boundaries. Dense windows with no trough keep iter_005's last-timestamp
rewind, making the change strictly additive over the current best.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> prompt channel (probed in iter_003) used as a STATIC
lexical-bias vector rather than a dynamic continuity feed: a fixed token-id
glossary prepended before <|startoftranscript|>, independent of any decoded
output.
what_i_learned:
generate's flat prompt list accepts [<|startofprev|>, *fixed_domain_ids,
*sot_prefix] — the same channel iter_003 used, but the content can be a
constant glossary with no feedback. This decouples lexical biasing from the
error-propagation loop that sank iter_003 (prev-window text re-injected its
own substitutions, cer 0.49); a static prior cannot compound errors window
to window, so the channel's biasing capability is separable from its
(failed) continuity use.
hypothesis:
The dominant axis is now substitution (56%, length_ratio 0.94 healthy) —
headroom is in WHAT is recognized (insurance domain terms, phone-band
audio), not coverage. Seeding the decoder with a high-frequency Korean
insurance call-center glossary biases token priors toward in-domain
vocabulary, lowering substitutions on domain terms without touching the
coverage machinery that iter_006 already fixed.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s **decoding_kwargs pass-through to ctranslate2 Whisper.generate —
specifically the WhisperGenerationOptions field no_repeat_ngram_size, a hard
in-decode constraint never set by any prior iteration (all anti-degeneracy
so far was iter_005's post-hoc temperature re-roll of a whole window).
what_i_learned:
The decode call accepts no_repeat_ngram_size in its kwargs: a per-decode hard
ban on re-emitting any n-gram, which acts WHILE the sequence forms rather than
after it (temperature fallback only re-rolls a completed window and cannot
interrupt a forming loop). This is a separate lever from sampling_temperature,
repetition_penalty, and beam_size, and is the only one of them that the
repeated_text guard violations (2 focus files, len down to 0.89) directly need.
hypothesis:
Set no_repeat_ngram_size=3 in every window decode. The two repeated_text
guard-violation files (00003092151 cer 0.227 len 0.89, 02_4038 cer 0.174) loop
on repeated phrases that both insert junk and delete real span; a trigram block
halts the loop in-decode while sparing 1-2 token natural Korean repeats,
lowering their cer without touching the healthy files.

capability_investigated:
The decoded text from result.sequences_ids[0] used as a degeneracy signal,
versus the scores[0] / no_speech_prob accept gates already wired in iter_005.
Specifically whether the temperature-fallback loop has any channel that can
detect a repetition loop, which the two repeated_text focus files exhibit.
what_i_learned:
scores[0] (avg log-prob) is blind to degeneracy: a repetition loop is
high-confidence per token, so a looping window posts a HIGH log-prob and
clears the -1.0 gate. The only orthogonal signal is the decoded text itself,
whose gzip compression ratio spikes on repetition — Whisper's native third
fallback trigger (compression_ratio_threshold), which the pipeline never
computed. This is why iter_008's blanket no_repeat_ngram ban (fired on every
window) lost ground while a surgical text-side gate need only touch loopers.
hypothesis:
Inside the existing per-window temperature loop, compute the candidate text's
gzip compression ratio and treat ratio > 2.4 as a failed decode: a window
stops climbing only when confident AND non-degenerate, and we prefer any
non-degenerate candidate over a degenerate one (ties broken by log-prob). A
confident loop is thus rejected and re-rolled at higher sampling temperature
(topk=0) which breaks it, fixing repeated_text on the focus files without the
global cost iter_008 paid; healthy windows still stop at greedy rung 1.

capability_investigated:
The <|startofprev|> long-form context channel of generate()'s flat prompt
list (probed iter_003) composed with the scores[0] log-prob gate and the
gzip-degeneracy signal (both wired in iter_005/iter_009) — i.e. whether a
per-window CONFIDENCE GATE can decide when prior decoded text is safe to
carry as decoder context, a composition no prior iteration built.
what_i_learned:
The prompt channel accepts [<|startofprev|>, *prev_text_ids, *sot] per
window, and the prior window's natural-text ids are recoverable from
sequences_ids[0] by keeping tokens with id < <|endoftext|> (timestamp and
special ids sit at/above it). iter_003 fed this blindly and compounded
substitutions (cer 0.49); the missing lever is that scores[0] and the
degeneracy ratio already give a per-window trust signal, so context can be
carried only from confident, non-degenerate windows and reset otherwise —
Whisper's native anti-drift design, which neither iter_003 (no gate) nor
iter_007 (static glossary, no real context) implemented.
hypothesis:
Substitution dominates (56%) with healthy coverage (len 0.94), so the
headroom is domain-term consistency, not coverage. Conditioning each window
on the prior CONFIDENT window's decoded text (capped to 200 tokens) carries
consistent insurance-term spellings forward, while the log-prob + degeneracy
gate resets context on any untrustworthy window so a bad decode cannot poison
successors the way iter_003's ungated feed did. No extra decode passes →
runtime budget unchanged.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s search mode and its N-best return channel: beam_size>1 with
num_hypotheses=N, and the resulting length-N scores / sequences_ids lists.
Also the cost asymmetry of whisper-large-v3-turbo (4 decoder layers vs 32
encoder layers) that makes beam search affordable within the runtime budget.
what_i_learned:
Every prior iter decoded greedily (beam_size=1) and read only scores[0] /
sequences_ids[0]. Setting num_hypotheses=N>1 makes generate RETURN the full
beam: scores and sequences_ids become length-N lists of competing
hypotheses, a return channel discarded until now. Because turbo's decoder is
only 4 layers against a 32-layer encoder (the per-window cost driver, run
once regardless of beam), widening the beam multiplies a cheap component, so
beam search is viable here. This directly addresses the substitution axis
(a token-search failure greedy cannot revisit) and lets the gzip-degeneracy
gate select a clean lower-ranked beam over a looping top-1.
hypothesis:
Replace the greedy first pass with a beam_size=5, num_hypotheses=5 decode and
select the best non-degenerate hypothesis (degeneracy gate, then log-prob
tie-break) across the whole returned beam. The temperature climb now fires
only when the entire beam fails the confidence/degeneracy gate. Beam search
is the canonical lever against substitution, and turbo's tiny decoder keeps
it inside the runtime budget. iter_006 windowing and iter_010 gated
long-form context are retained unchanged.

capability_investigated:
generate()'s beam_search patience factor (CT2 WhisperGenerationOptions
`patience`), a decode-search knob distinct from beam_size/num_hypotheses
that controls how long competing beams stay alive before pruning — never
set by any prior iteration (all ran at the default patience=1.0).
what_i_learned:
patience scales the live-beam pool to beam_size*patience: at the default 1.0
CT2 finalizes as soon as beam_size complete hypotheses exist, pruning
competitors a later token might have rescued. patience>1.0 defers that
pruning, so more acoustically-plausible token paths survive into the
returned N-best the degeneracy/log-prob selector already chooses from. It
multiplies only the cheap 4-layer decoder, not the once-per-window encoder,
so it stays inside the runtime budget.
hypothesis:
Substitution (57%, the dominant axis) is a search failure where the right
token loses to a locally-greedy competitor that pruning discards early.
Raising patience to 2.0 on the beam first pass keeps that competitor alive
longer, giving beam search a deeper search before commit and a richer N-best
for selection — a focused tune of the iter_011 parent, not a new mechanism.

capability_investigated:
The <|notimestamps|> control token as a per-window toggle. iter_004 only
established the global removal direction (drop it -> decoder emits timestamps
for the seek channel). The unused half is re-adding it conditionally so a
window decodes pure text with zero timestamp tokens, costing no extra encoder
pass (it is a prompt-prefix change on the single generate call already made).
what_i_learned:
generate()'s flat prompt accepts <|notimestamps|> appended after the task
token to suppress timestamp emission per window, and the seek channel is only
actually consumed on dense full windows (the last-timestamp rewind). Windows
cut at an acoustic silence trough (iter_006) or the final short chunk already
have a fixed seek, so they never read the timestamp channel — meaning the
timestamp tax they pay is pure waste and can be toggled off independently of
the dense-window seek path.
hypothesis:
Decoding silence_cut and final-chunk windows in clean-text mode lets the
distilled 4-layer turbo decoder spend its whole beam on text tokens instead
of interleaving 0.02 s position tokens, which should lower substitutions on
those windows (the mode Whisper is trained to transcribe in) while leaving
the dense worst-case files (which keep timestamp mode for the rewind)
unchanged, so it cannot regress them.

capability_investigated:
model.align() — a second method on the CT2 Whisper object returned by load(),
never called by any prior iteration (all used only generate()). It teacher-
forces a given token sequence against the audio via a DTW over the decoder
cross-attention and returns text_token_probs, a per-token posterior.
what_i_learned:
align() is reachable directly on load()'s model (no new import, no frozen
edit) and exposes a PER-TOKEN posterior channel that generate() never
surfaces: scores[0] is one window-level average and the gzip ratio is a whole-
text proxy, so neither can localise where inside a window a decode degraded.
A repetition-loop tail aligns to no fresh audio, so its per-token posterior
collapses while the clean head stays high — a localisable degeneracy signal.
hypothesis:
On windows the gzip gate still flags degenerate after the full beam+temperature
climb (a handful of windows, so the extra forward is cheap vs the per-window
encoder), run align() and drop the longest trailing run of sub-floor-posterior
tokens. This removes the loop tail the window-level gates kept whole, fixing
the two repeated_text focus files while leaving every healthy window untouched.
